summary.description: Benzene is a colourless, highly flammable liquid with a distinctive odour. It evaporates easily and is used in the production of many industrial products such as dyes, detergents, plastics, and pesticides. It is also present in petrol.
emission_sources: Production and industrial use in chemical manufacturing
Natural sources such as fires and volcanoes (minor contribution)
environmental_impact: Carcinogenic to humans under chronic exposure, affecting blood-forming organs
Contributes to formation of ground-level ozone, which harms respiratory health and leads to premature mortality
Ozone-related plant damage can reduce crop yields and forest growth
Potential contamination of soil and water

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Benzene is a known human carcinogen and chronic exposure can cause serious health problems, particularly affecting blood-forming organs and contributing to respiratory issues through ozone formation.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG11_Sustainable_Cities_and_Communities: Urban environments are major sources of benzene emissions due to vehicle traffic and industrial activity, making air quality and public health in cities particularly vulnerable.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Benzene's industrial use and environmental persistence call for more sustainable production processes and stricter regulation of hazardous chemicals to minimize exposure and environmental harm.
